recommendedApplyOrder.reasoning: Highest present-atom yield per unit of risk and by far the cheapest to run. The data is ALREADY IN THE STORE — a two-table read on one pool, no external API, no streaming, no rate limit, no vintage risk. 4,525,073 rows carry owner_name across 15 counties at 98.4% fill, so nearly every planned atom is a PRESENT atom rather than an absence. Carries the verify-by-PK fix (line 383). It is also the only one of the five that closes a named launch-gate hole: OPS-15 established OWN reads NO ATOM on the County Manifest while the data sat in cad_property unserved. Caveat to hold: owner-fact is public-paid, and the writer has an explicit leak guard at :342 ("Owner identity must never rest on the free tier") — confirm the gate honors accessPolicy before exposing. Risk is that it has no dry-run close artifact of its own, so run --limit dry-run on one county first; the store truth is well established but the rail's own behavior is undemonstrated.

Second-highest yield with a fully local data path — source is pre-loaded into tx_special_district, so applies are DB-to-DB with no network fetch, the fastest possible apply shape after owner-fact. Demonstrated 1,523,291 in-district present rows on Harris alone plus 10,932 on Bastrop, and coverage extends across all 196 parcel counties. RANKED BELOW OWNER DESPITE COMPARABLE VOLUME because of two real risks the planner must price. First, it is the ONLY rail of the five without any read-back verification — its verify is an in-memory schema self-check that cannot detect a failed write (see verifyFixEvidence), so an apply here is unaudited by construction; recommend porting the atom_did IN block from the sibling writers BEFORE applying, which is a small mechanical change against four working templates. Second, Harris emits ~4.1 memberships per in-district parcel, so 6.3M planned atoms on one county is a bulk-slot event that needs the throughput work (fc5a9c4 multi-row upsert) and a batch plan, not a casual run. Also note taxRate ships empty.

The safest rail technically and the best-demonstrated: it is the ONLY one of the five with non-zero present yield proven on TWO different counties (Bastrop 21 near / Dallas 16 near per 200-parcel sample), it carries the verify-by-PK fix (line 308), its source is a live federal layer with 16,522 TX segments confirmed by my own probe, and its licence is unrestricted US government work. Ranked third purely on volume, not quality: rail proximity is intrinsically sparse — roughly 8-10% of sampled parcels fall within the 152.4 m buffer — so the present-cell count is an order of magnitude below owner and special-district. Per-county apply requires a live ArcGIS fetch (55 corridors Bastrop, 850 Dallas) which adds a network dependency and ~12-20 s per 200 parcels, meaning statewide is a long but tractable run. Known honest gap: NET=T rail-trail is zero statewide, so that sub-class will never populate from this source.

Real data and a real present yield, but the compute cost per cell is catastrophic at the current algorithmic shape and that is what drops it to fourth. The Bastrop dry-run needed 1,762,884 ms (~29 minutes) to scan all 10,678,921 Texas features and join only 200 parcels; Dallas could not complete a join at all and was recorded as "O(footprints x parcels) prohibitive on 726k parcels". Every county re-streams the same 394 MB zip from Azure with no persisted table and no spatial index, so cost scales with statewide-features x county-parcels on EVERY run. Yield when it does run is decent (123 of 200 Bastrop parcels had a footprint, ~61%) and the source is live and statewide, so this rail is genuinely valuable — but it needs an engineering change first: persist the Texas footprints into a table with a GiST index (mirroring exactly what special-district already does with tx_special_district) and the cost collapses. Recommend deferring the apply and dispatching the ingest-table change; do not attempt a statewide apply in the current shape. Also note sourceTier is ml-derived, so confidence framing must not present these as surveyed.

DO NOT APPLY. This rail gains ZERO present cells in 253 of 254 counties and applying it would write pure absence at enormous volume. The source is a Harris County mirror, not a statewide RRC feed: 12,796 features total, 100% of them inside the Harris bbox, layer extent -95.94/29.51 to -94.90/30.17, projection wkid 2278 (Texas South Central), and the engine's own fetch-wells.ts:2 docstring says "Harris County mirror layer". The dry-runs already showed the consequence and it reproduces live — Dallas 693,556 planned / 0 present / 693,556 absent, Bexar 703,257 planned / 0 present / 703,257 absent, my own Dallas bbox probe returns count 0. Applying as-is would write ~1.4M absence atoms across two counties that assert 'no well on or near' as a machine-verified finding, when the truth is 'this source has no coverage here' — that is a correctness hazard, not merely a wasted run, because Texas genuinely has on the order of a million RRC wells and many of those counties DO have wells. The rail is well-built (verify-by-PK present at line 307, radius reasoning sound); only its source is wrong. Fix is a source swap to a genuinely statewide RRC feed, then re-dry-run. Until then this rail is code-done and customer-useless. Optionally apply to Harris (48201) ALONE, where the source is authoritative.

adversarialFindings: WELL-FACT'S SOURCE IS SINGLE-COUNTY AND NOTHING IN THE CLOSE ARTIFACT SAYS SO. The close recorded statewideCount 12796 / dallasBboxCount 0 / bexarBboxCount 0 and shipped anyway, treating the zeros as a legitimate absence result. Live probe 2026-08-11 proves the cause: returnExtentOnly in outSR=4326 is {-95.9402,29.5063,-94.8999,30.1740} and a Harris bbox query returns all 12,796 features. The field label 'statewideCount' in that artifact is itself misleading — it is a layer-total count, not statewide coverage. A rail whose absence atoms are indistinguishable from no-coverage is worse than an unbuilt rail.

SPECIAL-DISTRICT HAS NO READ-BACK VERIFICATION AT ALL AND WAS SILENTLY MISSED BY THE PK-FIX SWEEP. PRs #303/#304 fixed four writers; grep for `atom_did IN` returns hits at owner:383, rail-corridor:308, well:307, footprint:347 and ZERO in write-special-district-fact-county.mjs. Its verifyStoredSpecialDistrictFactAtom call passes the in-memory atom it just built, so verifyFailures can never be non-zero from a write failure. This is more dangerous than the old broken `body->>'atomDid'` form: the broken form was slow but real, this one is fast and fictional. Fix before applying — it is the largest-volume apply of the five (6.3M planned on Harris) and currently the only unaudited one.

THE PROMPT'S '~2,439 tax-relevant polygons' FIGURE IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. 2,775 polygons are loaded spanning all 17 TCEQ TYPE values (MUD 1888 is the plurality, not the whole), live TCEQ returns 2,796, and rateEnrichedCount is 0 on both dry-run counties — the Comptroller name join matched nothing. So ZERO loaded polygons are tax-enriched. 'Tax-relevant' should not appear in any external framing of this rail until the name reconciliation lands.

BUILDING-FOOTPRINT IS NOT APPLY-READY DESPITE A PASSING DRY-RUN. 29 minutes for 200 Bastrop parcels, and the Dallas full join was abandoned as prohibitive. The dry-run 'PASS' verdict measured correctness, not feasibility — a green regression line is masking an algorithm that cannot reach statewide. The irony is that the fix pattern already exists in this same PR wave: special-district persists its polygons to a table and queries per county, while footprint re-streams 394 MB and 10.7M features every single run.
